A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TWISTER research work, with 22 readable pages including Appendices A.1–A.7. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–21 are identical; the differences are confined to the first-page version stamp and Figure 12.

before.justification: v1 reports original TWISTER experiments on Atari 100k, component ablations, and 20 visual DeepMind Control tasks, including Tables 2, 3, 10, and 11.

after.justification: v2 retains those original Atari 100k, ablation, and DeepMind Control results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The Transformer world model, action-conditioned contrastive predictive coding objective, actor-critic learning, and architectural components are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 26 Atari 100k games and 20 visual DeepMind Control tasks. No training or evaluation domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains SimPLe, TWM, IRIS, DreamerV3, STORM, and Delta-IRIS. Table 11 retains DreamerPro, DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, and TWISTER without CPC; comparator participation is unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated evaluation procedures and training budgets are unchanged. Appendix A.7, Table 11, and Figure 12's caption already specify 1M environment steps in v1; correcting Figure 12's horizontal labels aligns the display with that existing budget rather than documenting a changed protocol.

E4.justification: The CPC-horizon, world-model architecture, action-conditioning, and augmentation ablations are identical. The latent-similarity analysis and qualitative prediction examples are also retained without changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-seed averaging, stratified bootstrap confidence intervals, and standard-deviation bands. Figure 12 retains its uncertainty bands and five-seed caption.

E6.justification: Figure 12 corrects the numerical step coordinates of the learning curves from 0/200K/400K to 0/500K/1M, changing the displayed association between scores and environment interactions. Curve shapes, score values, and rankings remain unchanged, including Table 11's TWISTER mean of 801.8 and median of 907.6.

T1.justification: The model definitions, loss equations, return calculations, and mathematical reasoning are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same AC-CPC contribution and performance claims, including Atari human-normalized mean and median scores of 162% and 77% and the qualification concerning methods without look-ahead search.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning longer-horizon prediction, attention to small objects, action conditioning, augmentation, and Transformer versus recurrent representations are unchanged. No limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Appendix architecture and hyperparameter Tables 4–9 are identical. Implementation descriptions and code-access information, including the linked destinations, are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and comparisons positioning TWISTER relative to prior world models and CPC are identical. No cited work or novelty relationship changes.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 6 March 2025 to v2 dated 25 May 2025. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 12 is redrawn with horizontal ticks labeled 0, 500K, and 1M instead of 0, 200K, and 400K across its task and aggregate panels, with slight spacing adjustments. Its caption and panel organization remain unchanged, as do all other figures and tables.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 12's step scale resolves its contradiction with the 1M-step budget already stated in Appendix A.7, Table 11, and the caption. This improves quantitative reporting by removing a misleading impression of sample efficiency. The methods, experimental evidence, final scores, and central conclusions remain unchanged.
